title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Pond and water-feature maintenance
audience: Pond and water-feature maintenance operators, including solo operators, starting or growing a residential or commercial water-feature service.
learningOutcomes: Write a pond or water-feature maintenance offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk a pond owner carries, and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will look after your pond' is a service. 'I will check the pump, the filter and the water level on each visit, clean the skimmer and pre-filter, send a short written note with photos, and return within the time we agree if the pump fails a check' is an offer. The owner buys a working system they can see, and the certainty that someone is checking it.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome, such as the pump and filter running at each visit, the skimmer and pre-filter clear, and the water level and clarity recorded. Set the time frame, such as a monthly or seasonal visit on a stated day. List what the client must do: give access, keep the power on, and tell you about any overflow after heavy rain. Give the certainty, which is the visit note with photos. Name the risk you carry, which is the return visit for a failed pump check. Put the scope and exclusions in writing. Exclusions for a pond offer usually include fish handling and any relocation of fish, liner repair, draining the whole pond, and plant removal. A written quote can become binding once it is accepted, so the exclusions protect both sides (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Fix the visit day. Tell the client in writing what to do with fish during a visit, so they do not decide on the day. Send one visit note that the client can read on a phone. Give one way to pay and one way to change a visit. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the client usually support a higher price, because the client is paying for convenience and reliability.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees apply to services, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services. A written workmanship warranty is an optional promise that sits on top of those rights (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Consumer Victoria's guidance says services must be done with due care and skill, but it does not set a fix-window length, so choose a window you can keep and state it. Do not promise fish health or water clarity, because those depend on feeding, weather, stock and the owner's own actions. Guarantee the visit, the check and the return visit instead. Any measured claim needs your own visit notes behind it.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. No published pond or water-feature maintenance price was found in the research, so do not quote a market rate. Set your price from your own cost and say on the quote how it was built. Good-better-best packages step up in price, with each level adding something the client can see, such as a filter clean or a seasonal pump service (Jobber Academy, updated 8 October 2024). Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as the Western Australian guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence a pond owner would repeat, such as 'the pump and filter running and the water checked at every visit'.
Set a visit interval you have checked against your own visit records, and record how often you meet it.
List what the client must do, such as giving access and keeping the power on, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: the visit note, the photos and a sign-off.
Decide the return-visit promise and check that you can afford the time it takes.
Price from value, set the price from your own cost, and state whether GST is included.

workedExamples.situation: A Queensland customer's koi pond overflows after heavy rain. The owner asks the business to drain it so the liner can be repaired, and asks whether the koi can be put in a holding tub and returned later. The research found no published pond price.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Write the offer for the drain and liner check, and decide what the offer excludes.
workedExamples.reasoning: The offer names the outcome: the pond drained to a level agreed with the owner, the liner checked, and a written note of the findings. It names the time frame and the client's inputs: access, power and a clear decision on the koi. It excludes the liner repair itself, which is quoted separately, and the relocation of the koi, which the owner arranges through a retailer or a new home. The offer does not discharge pond water into a drain or the environment. The Queensland fact sheet says ponds should not overflow into the environment, and its advice on tank water (which may carry eggs or larvae) is a reason to keep pond water out of drains. The fact sheet does not address ponds directly, so check the local council rule before the job.

equipmentAndPpe: Pond test kit or water-level and clarity log
Shared visit note template with photo fields

commonErrors.error: Guaranteeing fish health or water clarity that depends on feeding, weather or stock
commonErrors.prevention: Guarantee only what you control: the visit, the check, the return visit and your own workmanship.

commonErrors.error: Including the relocation or release of fish in an offer without checking the state rule
commonErrors.prevention: Exclude fish handling from the offer unless you have checked the rule for the state and the arrangement is written.

commonErrors.error: Quoting a market price for pond work when no source was checked
commonErrors.prevention: Set the price from your own cost and state the basis on the quote.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check your state's rules before acting.

Fish rules are state-based. Releasing fish is illegal in New South Wales without a permit, and Queensland says fish must never be released into waterways, wetlands or drains. In Victoria, koi need a permit to keep, transport or possess. Do not include fish moving, rehoming or release in an offer until you have checked the rule for the state where the pond is.
No licence requirement or trade-body source for pond and water-feature maintenance was confirmed in any state. This is a gap in the research, not a finding that no licence applies.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
Every offer shows its visit interval, what is included, what is excluded, and how each visit is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, a sample visit note, the evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A good pond offer promises a working system the operator checks, a fixed visit interval, a visit note and a fair return visit.
Higher rates follow from a visible check and reliable visits, not from longer hours.

Gap: no pond or water-feature maintenance price was found in a source with a stated figure. No trade-body or licence source for pond maintenance was found in any state. No current water-restriction rule for ornamental ponds was confirmed.
